div.b: SaaS or Hybrid changes exactly one of these five values

div.div:
SaaS base URL = https://aigw.portkey.ai
Prompts transit a Palo Alto Networks hosted endpoint.
Hybrid base URL = your in-cluster service, read from
kubectl get svc -n airs-gw (gateway port)
Prompts never leave your environment. The key, the slug, and the
model reference are identical, because they all come from the same
SCM tenant either way.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 654px; height: 1px; padding-top: 821px; margin-left: 717px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Worth saying out loud to the customer

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 841px; margin-left: 719px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
The gateway is opt-in per application. It is not a network
interception point: nothing is forced through it by routing, DNS, or
a proxy setting. An app that still points at the provider endpoint
keeps working and stays completely invisible to the gateway.
So coverage is an inventory problem, not a deployment problem.
Plan for how you will find and convert every AI caller, and how
you will stop new ones bypassing it — egress policy to the provider
endpoints, or revoking the direct provider keys once cut over.
